sources.title: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern
sources.version_commit: Living WAI-ARIA APG guidance; no page release/version stated.
sources.locator: About this pattern; autocomplete behaviors; Keyboard Interaction.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary W3C pattern page; compared manual-selection, automatic-selection, and Escape/arrow behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Popup is collapsed by default; editable combobox offers manual or automatic list selection; Escape dismisses a visible popup; popup descendants are outside the page Tab sequence.
sources.applicability: Web widget interaction reference only. Helps compare a filter input plus popup, but does not require ARIA in a native desktop app or guarantee AT behavior.

sources.title: WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog Pattern
sources.version_commit: Living WAI-ARIA APG guidance; no page release/version stated.
sources.locator: Keyboard Interaction; focus placement/return notes; WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary W3C dialog pattern; inspected initial focus, Tab containment, Escape, invoker focus return, and aria-modal conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Focus enters dialog on open, remains in a modal sequence, Escape closes, and returns to invoker unless removed/workflow warrants another destination. Modal semantics require outside interaction to be blocked for all users.
sources.applicability: Supports dismissal and focus-restoration requirements. Editor caret/selection restoration is an additional native-editor state concern.

sources.title: WAI-ARIA APG Listbox Pattern
sources.version_commit: Living WAI-ARIA APG guidance; no page release/version stated.
sources.locator: About; Keyboard Interaction; roles/states/properties and notes.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary W3C pattern; reviewed selection/focus distinction, arrow navigation, option naming, and nested-control limitations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Single-select listbox focus may optionally follow selection; long option names are spoken as a unit; listbox interaction does not operate nested buttons/links.
sources.applicability: Use to evaluate concise single-action rows and separate focus from invocation; do not pack nested actions into a listbox option.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.version_commit: WCAG 2.2 supporting Understanding document; living page, no separate page version stated.
sources.locator: In Brief; Success Criterion; Intent.
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C guidance and reviewed non-focus status communication and avoiding unnecessary interruption.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Status changes that do not receive focus should be programmatically determinable for AT; intent includes informing without unnecessarily interrupting.
sources.applicability: Supports concise polite result/status announcements. It does not set an exact debounce interval or guarantee a particular screen-reader utterance.

sources.title: VS Code 1.137.0 command palette provider

sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned kernel documentation and inspected memory accounting, limit, peak and delegation text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: memory.current counts cgroup and descendants, memory.peak tracks maximum since cgroup creation/reset; memory.high throttles/reclaims but may be breached and does not invoke OOM killer; memory.max is hard but may be exceeded temporarily and can invoke OOM kill inside the cgroup. sources.locator: Single-writer rule; hierarchy support; Delegation; controller enablement
sources.observed_operation: Read systemd guidance on ownership/delegation and version-specific hierarchy transitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: cgroup v2 is governed by a single-writer rule; direct management outside the delegated subtree is not allowed. Delegate is available to services/scopes, but setting it makes requested controllers available without enabling them; enable memory in the delegated subtree. systemd documentation says legacy/hybrid hierarchies deprecated in v256 and removed in v258.

sources.locator: Struct Semaphore overview; acquire_many; cancel safety
sources.observed_operation: Read published API contract for permits, FIFO behavior and acquire_many interactions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Waiters receive permits in FIFO request order, including acquire_many; a large request at queue head can block smaller requests despite available permits. Cancelling acquire loses its position.
sources.applicability: Useful bounded-concurrency primitive example; does not persist tenant queue state, explain wait reasons, or enforce byte memory limits.

sources.locator: module implementation comments and waiter queue; permit assignment and cancellation cleanup around lines 1-16, 280-355, 380-515, 570-611
sources.observed_operation: Opened raw source at exact release tag; reviewed linked waiter queue, FIFO order and drop cleanup behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Implementation uses intrusive waiter list, places waiters at tail and assigns released permits from head; Acquire::drop removes waiter/returns assigned permits. This implementation governs Tokio's in-process semaphore, not durable host jobs.
sources.applicability: Inspected as a candidate primitive's real implementation, not selected as the task scheduler.

sources.observed_operation: Opened issue page and read reproducer/context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter observes a spawned task not progressing when another task loops acquiring a permit without a cooperative yield; issue links to #4624. This is a runtime/task-cooperation report, not evidence of broken semaphore FIFO.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL permits reader/writer overlap but only one writer; all users must be on same host and WAL is unsupported over network filesystems. sources.title: Transaction — SQLite
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE modes

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately and may fail SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active; deferred read-to-write upgrade may fail later.
sources.applicability: Supports short transactional CAS/state transitions in an embedded local queue; caller still handles busy and never wraps long-running work in a transaction.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: memory.current covers a cgroup and descendants; memory.peak tracks maximum use since creation/reset. memory.high throttles/reclaims but may be exceeded and does not invoke OOM; memory.max is the hard control but may be exceeded temporarily and can invoke OOM inside the cgroup. sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux kernel documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Linux kernel documentation tree 7.1; API behavior must be verified on supported installed kernels
sources.locator: Delegation section lines 174–179; memory interface lines 639–707; memory events lines 751–785
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned kernel docs; inspected delegation model, memory.high/max, memory.current/peak and events.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Controller files are exposed only if controller is available/enabled; delegating access requires parent permissions; memory.high throttles and does not invoke OOM; memory.max is a hard limit that invokes cgroup OOM when reclaim fails, can temporarily be exceeded; major usage accounting is stated to be reasonable rather than fully watertight.
sources.applicability: Supports capability-gated Linux worker memory limits and event-based measurement; no-admin deployment can use only a writable pre-delegated cgroup. OOM action is scoped to cgroup per docs.

sources.locator: Members ProcessMemoryLimit and JobMemoryLimit, lines 54–72 in opened documentation
sources.observed_operation: Opened API reference and inspected fields and remarks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PROCESS_MEMORY and JOB_MEMORY limits bound virtual memory that can be committed, not RSS/physical memory. Job and per-process commit limits are independent. Notification-limit path can notify while allowing further commits.
sources.applicability: Supports Windows task-descendant committed-memory boundary and calibration; UI must not equate commit cap with physical RAM cap.

sources.title: AssignProcessToJobObject

sources.locator: Remarks on existing job, access rights, same session and older Windows versions; lines 51–70
sources.observed_operation: Opened API reference and inspected assignment constraints and OS-version exceptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Assignment requires a job with assign rights and a process handle with quota/terminate rights. Already-jobbed processes must fit a valid nested hierarchy and cannot use UI limits; before Windows 8 the process could not already be in a job. All processes in a job must be in the same Terminal Services session.
sources.applicability: Requires launch-time capability probe; do not assume a worker can be added to a job in every host environment.

sources.title: HTTP Semantics
sources.version: RFC 9110, Standards Track, June 2022; current errata must be checked before implementation
sources.locator: §§ 8.8.1–8.8.3 (validators and ETag); 9.3.2 (HEAD); 13.1.2–13.1.3 (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since)
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the RFC; inspected section text for validators, conditional requests, 304 behavior, HEAD, and modification dates.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: ETag is an opaque server-chosen validator; it is weak unless marked strong. If-None-Match uses weak comparison, primarily for conditional GET and can produce 304 when the supplied tag matches. Last-Modified comparison is implicitly weak unless stringent conditions are met; If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present and in several invalid/inapplicable cases. HEAD carries no representation body and reports metadata that would accompany GET.
sources.applicability: Basis for optional, conditional upstream revalidation and honest status labels; does not establish product release identity, semantic applicability, or claim truth.

sources.title: HTTP Caching
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the RFC; inspected freshness calculation, disconnected use, validation, and response update conditions.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Freshness is cache reuse without validation, determined by explicit max-age/Expires or permitted heuristic rules. Freshness applies to cache operation and does not force an application display refresh. Stale responses can be served in specified disconnected/explicitly permitted conditions, but must-revalidate forbids reuse while stale and disconnected. A 304 updates eligible stored response metadata under validator/key matching rules.
sources.applicability: Separates cache freshness and offline usability from handbook evidence status; supports preserving cached versions and recording revalidation events.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.version: W3C Recommendation, 23 February 2017 (stable recommendation; publication page says other documents may supersede it)
sources.locator: §§ 3.2.3, 4.2.4 Text Quote Selector, 4.2.5 Text Position Selector, 4.3 States
sources.observed_operation: Opened the W3C Recommendation and reviewed model and selector sections and examples.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A quote selector stores normalized exact text and may include immediately preceding/following context. Text positions use normalized Unicode code points, end-exclusive; positions are explicitly brittle under edits/dynamic content, for which a State is recommended. When exact/prefix/suffix yield multiple matches, the model says the selector should be treated as matching all of them. The spec warns that copying large text into shared annotations can be rights-sensitive.
sources.applicability: Useful, interoperable shape for a local passage anchor: short exact/context quote plus offsets and source snapshot/parser identity; ambiguous matches must stay ambiguous. It is not a revision identity scheme.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.locator: § 3.2 expanded terms: wasQuotedFrom, wasRevisionOf, specializationOf, alternateOf; §§ 3.1–3.2 entity/activity relationships
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Recommendation and inspected the derivation and entity-relationship definitions.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: wasRevisionOf means the derived entity retains substantial content from the original; wasQuotedFrom describes content repeated from a possibly larger entity; specializationOf relates a more specific, time/context-specific entity to a general one; alternateOf relates aspects of the same thing that need not be identical in aspect or time.
sources.applicability: Guides typed provenance edges so the system does not label a URL redirect, byte variant, release, or superseding document as the same relation.

sources.title: Git core data model
sources.version: Rolling online documentation; page does not expose a release pin, reviewed 12 October 2026 UTC
sources.locator: OBJECTS and REFERENCES sections, especially object IDs, commits, branches, and tags
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official Git documentation and reviewed object and ref semantics.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Git objects are immutable after creation and named by a hash of type and contents; a commit names a tree and parents. Branch references move as new commits are made; tags usually do not change, but are refs rather than a general proof that the vendor’s stated version is authentic.
sources.applicability: Excellent exact locator for docs hosted in Git when the full commit plus repository/path is retained; inadequate for non-repository sites and release labels alone.

sources.title: Getting permanent links to files
sources.version: Rolling GitHub documentation, reviewed 12 October 2026 UTC
sources.locator: Sections “File views show the latest version on a branch” and “Press Y to permalink to a file in a specific commit”
sources.observed_operation: Opened current official documentation and inspected pinned vs branch URL guidance.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A branch URL displays its current head and may change; replacing the branch segment with a commit ID pins exact file content, and line/range links can identify a code passage. The behavior applies to GitHub repository files.
sources.applicability: Practical result-link format for repository-hosted handbooks/docs; source commit remains separate from the requested product/version.

sources.title: Software Heritage persistent identifiers
sources.version: Software Heritage documentation version 1.6, last modified 30 April 2021 (as stated on page); rolling docs URL
sources.locator: Overview, syntax, semantics, context qualifiers (origin/visit/anchor/path) and fragment qualifier (lines)
sources.observed_operation: Searched the official Software Heritage docs and inspected the indexed specification text; direct open later returned an access-denied page, so specific-version semantics are based on the search-exposed page text, not an independent full-page fetch.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: SWHIDs identify archived software objects (snapshot/release/revision/directory/content) by intrinsic object identifiers and may carry origin, visit, anchor, path, or line qualifiers. The reviewed v1.6 spec uses SHA-1 Git-style object hashes. Identifier stability does not by itself promise that a target document is archived or that the archive resolver is online.
sources.applicability: Useful optional identifier/archive route for code and repository docs; not a default for arbitrary web pages and not a reason to adopt its SHA-1 scheme for new local digests.

sources.title: HTTP Framework for Time-Based Access to Resource States (Memento)
sources.locator: §§ 2.1–2.2 (Memento-Datetime and relation types), § 3 (datetime negotiation)
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the RFC; inspected Memento/TimeGate/TimeMap and temporal navigation relations.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Memento-Datetime labels a response as reflecting a prior state; Accept-Datetime requests date negotiation through a TimeGate. The protocol can navigate archived states where an archive implements it; it does not force coverage, guarantee availability, or define the vendor’s product release.
sources.applicability: Optional fallback discovery route for relocated/disappeared public pages, explicitly shown as an archive copy and never silently substituted for a product-specific official source.

sources.title: Secure Hash Standard
sources.locator: § 1 and SHA-256 algorithm definition
sources.observed_operation: Searched NIST’s publication repository for the standard and reviewed the indexed text.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The standard specifies SHA-256 among secure hash algorithms and describes message digests as useful for detecting message changes with very high probability; a digest is an integrity fingerprint, not proof of origin, provenance, or meaning.
sources.applicability: Supports storing algorithm-tagged local byte fingerprints for exact cached payload comparison, alongside (not instead of) source/version metadata.

sources.title: Select best match for quote selectors in PDFs when position-based anchoring fails
sources.version: hypothesis/client issue #3705, opened 24 August 2021; resolved by merged PR #3743
sources.locator: Issue description, particularly interaction of position hint, page search order, fuzzy score threshold and early return
sources.observed_operation: Opened the public issue. The report says PDF.js text extraction can shift across versions and first sufficiently close match may be returned even when a better match occurs elsewhere.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Problem is specific to PDF text extraction and the cited anchoring implementation: positions can become unreliable across PDF.js versions; approximate match threshold and search order can select a wrong passage before the global best candidate.
sources.applicability: Concrete caution against silent fuzzy reattachment and against treating a position as durable. It is one product’s issue report, not proof all anchor systems have the same bug.

independent_primary_source_rechecks.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Vary lists request fields that may select response content; Vary:* can reflect unlisted request aspects and a recipient cannot determine later appropriateness without forwarding to origin. independent_primary_source_rechecks.title: HTTP Caching

independent_primary_source_rechecks.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Reuse without revalidation requires nominated Vary request fields to match the original request; absent fields match only absent fields and Vary:* always fails a cache match. sources.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
sources.source_type: IETF Standards Track RFC; primary protocol specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 9110, STD 97, published June 2022
sources.locator: §8.8.1–8.8.3 (validators, Last-Modified, ETag); §13.1.2–13.1.3 (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since); §15.4.5 (304); §12.5.5 Vary; §15.4.5 304 Not Modified
sources.observed_operation: web__run search/open/find on the official RFC HTML; no request was sent to a case URL.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Last-Modified reports the origin server's believed modification time of the selected representation; the determination is implementation-specific.
Last-Modified is implicitly weak unless RFC clock/resolution conditions permit it to be treated as strong.
ETag is an opaque validator for selected representations, not necessarily a cryptographic digest.
If-None-Match uses weak comparison for GET cache validation, so matching may validate even if representation data changed.
If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present; dates are fallback validators, not proof of byte identity.

Vary identifies request fields that may have selected the response representation; it expands the matching key, and Vary:* means the variant may depend on other factors the client cannot fully reproduce.
A 304 response has no content body and returns only specified metadata for cache updates; it is not the new representation body and cannot itself re-resolve passage anchors.
sources.applicability: Defines online-check claims; keep validator outcome separate from local byte hash, source version and claim applicability. Record the selected representation's media type/language, Vary fields and safe variant inputs; treat Vary:* or non-reproducible selection as variant-unknown.

additional_access_events.observed_operation: web__run opened RFC 9110 §12.5.5 and §15.4.5 and found Vary/304 passages.

governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A cache may calculate heuristic freshness only when explicit freshness is absent and the response is eligible; Last-Modified can inform an estimate.
Freshness is cache-reuse policy, and successful validation can update cache metadata; neither determines whether a technical claim applies to a release.
Conditional validators support cache revalidation; handbook evidence semantics are a separate layer.
sources.applicability: Avoid presenting cache-fresh/cache-stale policy as a conclusion about note validity.

sources.locator: §4.2.4 Text Quote Selector; §4.2.5 Text Position Selector; §4.3 States; §4.3.1 Time State; §4.3.2 Request Header State

governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: TextQuoteSelector stores normalized exact text and may store prefix/suffix context.
TextPositionSelector uses normalized Unicode code-point offsets, zero-based with end exclusive.
Position selectors are brittle under edits; the Recommendation recommends an additional State to identify the correct representation.

sources.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
sources.source_type: IETF Standards Track RFC; primary protocol specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 9110, STD 97, published June 2022
sources.locator: §8.8.1–8.8.3 (validators, Last-Modified, ETag); §13.1.2–13.1.3 (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since); §15.4.5 (304); §12.5.5 Vary; §15.4.5 304 Not Modified
sources.observed_operation: web__run search/open/find on the official RFC HTML; no request was sent to a case URL.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Last-Modified reports the origin server's believed modification time of the selected representation; the determination is implementation-specific.
Last-Modified is implicitly weak unless RFC clock/resolution conditions permit it to be treated as strong.
ETag is an opaque validator for selected representations, not necessarily a cryptographic digest.
If-None-Match uses weak comparison for GET cache validation, so matching may validate even if representation data changed.
If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present; dates are fallback validators, not proof of byte identity.

Vary identifies request fields that may have selected the response representation; it expands the matching key, and Vary:* means the variant may depend on other factors the client cannot fully reproduce.
A 304 response has no content body and returns only specified metadata for cache updates; it is not the new representation body and cannot itself re-resolve passage anchors.
sources.applicability: Defines online-check claims; keep validator outcome separate from local byte hash, source version and claim applicability. Record the selected representation's media type/language, Vary fields and safe variant inputs; treat Vary:* or non-reproducible selection as variant-unknown.

additional_access_events.observed_operation: web__run opened RFC 9110 §12.5.5 and §15.4.5 and found Vary/304 passages.
Independent critic web__run open/find on RFC Editor HTML §§8.8.1–8.8.3, 12.5.5, 13.1.2, 15.4.2–15.4.9: validators, Vary, 304, and redirect status meanings.

Reviser web__run open/find on RFC Editor RFC 9110 §§8.8.1, 13.1.2, 15.4.2–15.4.9; checked strong-validator definition, weak If-None-Match comparison, required 304 metadata/no body, and redirect status distinctions.

governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A cache may calculate heuristic freshness only when explicit freshness is absent and the response is eligible; Last-Modified can inform an estimate.
Freshness is cache-reuse policy, and successful validation can update cache metadata; neither determines whether a technical claim applies to a release.
Conditional validators support cache revalidation; handbook evidence semantics are a separate layer.
sources.applicability: Avoid presenting cache-fresh/cache-stale policy as a conclusion about note validity.

A hash alone does not prove publisher identity, semantic version or applicability; a hash does not protect confidentiality.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.released_version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation dated 2017-02-23
sources.locator: §4.2.4 Text Quote Selector; §4.2.5 Text Position Selector; §4.3 States; §4.3.1 Time State; §4.3.2 Request Header State
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened the dated Recommendation and selector anchors; find located selector definitions and brittleness note.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: TextQuoteSelector stores normalized exact text and may store prefix/suffix context.
TextPositionSelector uses normalized Unicode code-point offsets, zero-based with end exclusive.
Position selectors are brittle under edits; the Recommendation recommends an additional State to identify the correct representation.
A State describes how to retrieve the intended representation; Time State can identify a historical representation and Request Header State describes headers for the intended variant.
A response representation may also depend on non-header context such as client IP; recording headers may not be sufficient to recreate it.
sources.applicability: Use quote/context plus edition identity and structural locator; position is only a hint within the pinned edition. Keep copied note excerpts local. Store only safe representation-selection metadata needed for public sources; never persist/replay credentials or unrelated private headers.

Durability depends on storage/VFS/hardware assumptions; no multi-file package-and-database transaction is implied.
sources.applicability: Use record-sized transactions, avoid claiming atomicity across media copy and database state, and fault-test the actual environment.

sources.locator: §§3.7–3.11 commit sequence; stated storage and flush assumptions.
sources.observed_operation: Read the official commit explanation and conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Atomicity depends on database journaling, flushes and storage/VFS/hardware assumptions. It does not imply an atomic transaction across the application database and separately copied package files.
sources.applicability: Supports MI-01 and the draft's own caveat about cross-filesystem/database recovery.

sources.title: SQLite transaction documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current official documentation; page last updated 2026-02-18; SQLite runtime version not captured.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1–2.2: read/write transactions, DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE, SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official transaction page and read its transaction and writer-concurrency sections in a read-only browser review.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple simultaneous read transactions are allowed, with only one simultaneous write transaction. A DEFERRED read-to-write upgrade or IMMEDIATE start can return SQLITE_BUSY. This describes database transactions.
sources.applicability: Supports serial database checkpoint writes and explicit busy/recovery handling if SQLite is chosen; it does not certify external package operations.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current official documentation; article describes rollback-journal mode and says WAL uses a different mechanism; SQLite runtime version not captured.
sources.locator: Sections 1–2 and 3.7–3.11: atomic transaction scope, journal mode, storage/flush assumptions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official atomic-commit explanation and read its scope and hardware-assumption sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page describes all-or-none changes within a database transaction under stated storage and flush assumptions. Its detailed mechanism is rollback mode; WAL uses another mechanism. It makes no statement that separate application package files participate in a database transaction.
sources.applicability: Supports limiting the proposal’s database atomicity claim; the conclusion that unrelated package filesystem operations are outside that database transaction is an application-boundary inference.

sources.title: Rust std::fs::rename
sources.version_or_commit: Rust standard-library documentation 1.97.0; source commit 2d8144b78, dated 2026-07-07 on page.
sources.locator: Function description and Platform-specific behavior, especially rename replacement, cross-mount failure, and Unix/Windows differences.
sources.condition: A rename is one filesystem operation; behavior differs by platform and fails across mount points. Do not infer atomicity across a separate manifest/database update.
sources.applicability: Keep staging and final paths on the same target filesystem; verify behavior on each supported OS and reconcile a crash between file finalization and manifest commit.
sources.observed_operation: web__run search_query and open on the official Rust standard-library rename documentation.
sources.time_basis: Clock timestamp captured immediately after the web research group; web__run does not expose per-request timestamps.

sources.title: POSIX rename specification
sources.version_or_commit: The Open Group Base Specifications Issue 8, POSIX.1-2024; live standards page.
sources.locator: rename() rationale: the action of the function is required to be atomic; description and error conditions.
sources.condition: The atomicity statement applies to a conforming POSIX rename operation on that filesystem; it says nothing about Windows behavior or atomic coordination with a separate database transaction. Search results exposed the relevant excerpt; direct page open returned HTTP 403.
sources.applicability: Evidence for treating a single POSIX rename as an operation boundary, while still designing restart reconciliation across independent resources.
sources.observed_operation: web__run search_query on the official Open Group POSIX rename page; follow-up open returned 403 Forbidden.
sources.time_basis: Clock timestamp captured immediately after the web research group; web__run does not expose per-request timestamps.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit
sources.version_or_commit: Current official SQLite documentation; page not release-stamped.
sources.locator: Introduction and sections 3.11–3.12 on transaction commit; section 8 on crash tests; rollback-mode/WAL qualification.
sources.condition: SQLite describes atomic commit for database transaction changes, including crash/power-loss handling subject to filesystem/OS assumptions; the detailed algorithm at the page's start is for rollback mode, with WAL using another mechanism.
sources.applicability: A local manifest row can be transactionally committed, but this guarantee does not cover a separate media file; inject faults at the boundary between the file operation and row transaction.
sources.observed_operation: web__run open on the official SQLite atomic-commit page.
sources.time_basis: Clock timestamp captured immediately after the web research group; web__run does not expose per-request timestamps.

sources.title: ffprobe Documentation
sources.version_commit: Online FFmpeg documentation, live page accessed 2026-10-12; related current stable release S01
sources.locator: Description; -show_format, -show_streams, -show_error, -of json, -formats/-demuxers/-codecs; JSON optional-field behavior

sources.title: FFmpeg Formats Documentation
sources.version_commit: Online FFmpeg documentation, live page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Input options analyzeduration and duration_probesize; format_whitelist; probe defaults

sources.applicability: Record probe limits and duration provenance; bounded metadata extraction needs explicit timeout/uncertain duration states.

sources.title: GStreamer audioconvert plugin reference
sources.version_commit: Live plugin reference; audioconvert is in gst-plugins-base, stable series 1.28.8 at access
sources.locator: mix-matrix example; channel reordering for unpositioned inputs; package and raw-audio pad templates
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official GStreamer plugin page and read matrix/reordering examples.
sources.condition_default_exception: The mix matrix explicitly maps input to output channels; unpositioned inputs can be automatically positioned by channel index or forced into a chosen standard layout. This transforms decoded audio in the preview pipeline and can change speaker interpretation.
sources.applicability: Evidence that channel-selective preview is feasible in a decoded pipeline; preserve the original file, do not assume mapping or export the transformed preview as source.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit
sources.version_commit: Live official SQLite technical documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Transaction atomicity after crash/power failure; assumptions about fsync and locks; sections 3, 8, and 9.1
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation and searched crash/power-loss and transaction atomicity details.
sources.condition_default_exception: Transactions appear atomic under the documented filesystem/VFS assumptions; broken flush/fsync can undermine it, and documentation warns against using SQLite on network filesystems because locking may be broken.
sources.applicability: Suitable candidate for local per-item resume journal only on local storage with documented durability settings; do not store active job DB on network share.

sources.title: GStreamer Audio Channel Positions
sources.version_commit: Live GStreamer API reference accessed 2026-10-12; channel API includes stable 1.x elements
sources.locator: Channel-mask conversion; channel-position rules; mono/position-less/two-channel no-mask conventions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official audio channel API docs and reviewed channel-position semantics.
sources.condition_default_exception: A channel mask of zero means positions absent; two channels without a mask conventionally imply front-left/front-right in GStreamer audio caps, not speaker identity.
sources.applicability: Do not automatically call left/right channels interviewer/narrator. Preserve raw indices and distinguish technical positions from staff labels.

sources.title: GStreamer Modules
sources.version_commit: Official module index accessed 2026-10-12; stable modules listed as 1.28.8, development 1.29.2
sources.locator: Module table for core, gst-plugins-base, good, ugly, bad, gst-libav, and Cerbero
sources.observed_operation: Opened official module index and reviewed current stable versions and module descriptions.
sources.condition_default_exception: GStreamer is divided into independently versioned modules; many users need core/base/good, while other plugin groups and gst-libav are separate.
sources.applicability: A GStreamer parser/preview capability report must identify each installed module/version, not merely the core runtime.

sources.title: GStreamer Download and platform packaging page
sources.version_commit: Official download page accessed 2026-10-12; page listed 1.28.7 installers while module/release pages listed 1.28.8
sources.locator: Platform installers, toolchain compatibility, Linux/BSD package notes, distribution plugin omissions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official download page and reviewed platform-specific bundle and distribution-package notes.
sources.condition_default_exception: The live page states distributions may split packages or omit bad/ugly/libav plugin modules; at access it still listed 1.28.7 installers, a lag behind the stable module index at 1.28.8.
sources.applicability: A bundle update can lag the framework's stable release; verify the exact platform package includes fixed module versions before relying on its capabilities.

sources.title: GStreamer audioconvert plugin reference
sources.version_commit: Live plugin reference; audioconvert is in gst-plugins-base, stable series 1.28.8 at access
sources.locator: mix-matrix example; channel reordering for unpositioned inputs; package and raw-audio pad templates
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official GStreamer plugin page and read matrix/reordering examples.
sources.condition_default_exception: The mix matrix explicitly maps input to output channels; unpositioned inputs can be automatically positioned by channel index or forced into a chosen standard layout. This transforms decoded audio in the preview pipeline and can change speaker interpretation.
sources.applicability: Evidence that channel-selective preview is feasible in a decoded pipeline; preserve the original file, do not assume mapping or export the transformed preview as source.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit
sources.version_commit: Live official SQLite technical documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Transaction atomicity after crash/power failure; assumptions about fsync and locks; sections 3, 8, and 9.1
sources.observed_operation: Opened official documentation and searched crash/power-loss and transaction atomicity details.
sources.condition_default_exception: Transactions appear atomic under the documented filesystem/VFS assumptions; broken flush/fsync can undermine it, and documentation warns against using SQLite on network filesystems because locking may be broken.
sources.applicability: Suitable candidate for local per-item resume journal only on local storage with documented durability settings; do not store active job DB on network share.

sources.title: GStreamer Audio Channel Positions
sources.version_commit: Live GStreamer API reference accessed 2026-10-12; channel API includes stable 1.x elements
sources.locator: Channel-mask conversion; channel-position rules; mono/position-less/two-channel no-mask conventions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official audio channel API docs and reviewed channel-position semantics.
sources.condition_default_exception: A channel mask of zero means positions absent; two channels without a mask conventionally imply front-left/front-right in GStreamer audio caps, not speaker identity.
sources.applicability: Do not automatically call left/right channels interviewer/narrator. Preserve raw indices and distinguish technical positions from staff labels.

sources.title: GStreamer Modules
sources.version_commit: Official module index accessed 2026-10-12; stable modules listed as 1.28.8, development 1.29.2
sources.locator: Module table for core, gst-plugins-base, good, ugly, bad, gst-libav, and Cerbero
sources.observed_operation: Opened official module index and reviewed current stable versions and module descriptions.
sources.condition_default_exception: GStreamer is divided into independently versioned modules; many users need core/base/good, while other plugin groups and gst-libav are separate.
sources.applicability: A GStreamer parser/preview capability report must identify each installed module/version, not merely the core runtime.

sources.title: GStreamer Download and platform packaging page
sources.version_commit: Official download page accessed 2026-10-12; page listed 1.28.7 installers while module/release pages listed 1.28.8
sources.locator: Platform installers, toolchain compatibility, Linux/BSD package notes, distribution plugin omissions
sources.observed_operation: Opened official download page and reviewed platform-specific bundle and distribution-package notes.
sources.condition_default_exception: The live page states distributions may split packages or omit bad/ugly/libav plugin modules; at access it still listed 1.28.7 installers, a lag behind the stable module index at 1.28.8.
sources.applicability: A bundle update can lag the framework's stable release; verify the exact platform package includes fixed module versions before relying on its capabilities.

sources.observed_operation: Searched official FFmpeg manual; opened tagged source; read relevant option and writer sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Output format can be JSON; stream and container info are separate sections; error info appears when -show_error is requested; JSON may omit invalid/non-applicable values in auto policy.
sources.applicability: Candidate local metadata probe and machine-readable output. Field absence cannot establish source absence; pin build/config and validate relevant files.

sources.locator: FFPROBE_COMMAND and FFPROBE_OUTPUT_MODES_TESTS; synthetic NUT fixture; writers include JSON; source lines 258-280.
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged test makefile and inspected fixture/targets.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Test exercises ffprobe output writers including json with streams, packets, format, and frames on generated test input; it is project regression coverage, not a guarantee for all formats or museum media.
sources.applicability: Evidence that JSON interface is tested; supports proposal to add local test corpus, not claim that tests were run here.

sources.title: FFmpeg libavformat format options
sources.released_version_or_commit: FFmpeg n8.1.1 tag
sources.locator: Format Options: probesize (lines 799-807); analyzeduration (lines 899-904).
sources.observed_operation: Opened official tagged source and read option defaults/descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: probesize is 5,000,000 bytes by default; analyzeduration is 5,000,000 microseconds (5 seconds) by default. Larger values can detect more dispersed information but increase latency.
sources.applicability: Duration/stream probe completeness and 500-file latency must be evaluated; avoid treating a bounded probe's omission as a negative fact.

sources.released_version_or_commit: MediaInfo v26.10, release commit f057dd3
sources.locator: Release notes, especially Opus 5.0/center-channel ordering fix and MP3 headerless VBR detection after parsing.
sources.observed_operation: Opened release tag and read release metadata and notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release history records parser behavior fixes; a later release may change parsing, so record exact version and rerun representative samples after upgrades.
sources.applicability: Evidence for version pinning and channel/duration regression fixtures; not a support guarantee for any particular collection.

sources.title: MediaInfoLib audio stream field definitions

sources.locator: Audio fields Channel(s), ChannelPositions, ChannelLayout, SamplingRate, SamplingCount, Source_SamplingCount.
sources.observed_operation: Opened released tag source and inspected audio-field definitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Field definitions distinguish channel count, reported positions, layout, and sample counts; defined fields may be unavailable or inferred differently for a format.
sources.applicability: Useful normalization candidates. Preserve raw fields and do not infer speaker identity from count/layout.

sources.title: MediaInfo open duration discrepancy issue
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue #373, opened 2019-08-16; no release tag applies; observed Open at access.
sources.locator: Issue description includes QuickTime/MOV example and conflicting tkhd/mdhd duration fields.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream issue; read current status and sample report.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report describes inconsistent container and audio-track durations; user notes audio appears intact. Issue is an example, not proof all duration conflicts are parser bugs.
sources.applicability: Keep duration source and scope; if values conflict, surface both and request review rather than silently choosing.

sources.title: MediaInfo JSON cardinality issue and proposed fix
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue #1103 and linked MediaInfoLib PR #2295 / commit d2d4c05; PR still Open and unmerged at access.
sources.locator: Issue description documents object for one CLI input vs array for 2+; PR conversation/commit proposes uniform array.
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and linked PR; read status, proposal, and commit reference.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The described difference occurs across invocation cardinality. A proposed change is not a released fix while its PR remains open.
sources.applicability: For integration, invoke one file at a time or normalize and schema-check JSON with the exact deployed version.

sources.title: Siegfried signature-based identification documentation and release
sources.released_version_or_commit: Siegfried v1.11.9, release commit 7fb430b
sources.locator: About/signature support; JSON/CSV/DROID outputs; Signature files (default latest PRONOM signatures, no buffer limits; potentially full-file scans); -update behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened released README and release page; inspected supported signature families and default scanning behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Signature matching uses an independently updated signature file; default may scan entire files. The exact signature-file database version is not identified by the README snapshot.
sources.applicability: Optional preservation-oriented identity layer; freeze binary plus signature file/version/hash. It does not establish readability, duration, or preview support.

sources.title: libsndfile 1.2.2 API and supported formats
sources.released_version_or_commit: libsndfile 1.2.2 tag
sources.locator: File Open Function / SF_INFO fields; read-only SFM_READ; RAW exception requiring caller-supplied samplerate, channels, and format; formats list.
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged API docs and supported-format documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SF_INFO exposes frames, samplerate, channels, format; on read, fields are filled by library except RAW which requires caller parameters. Supported format/encoding combinations are finite.
sources.applicability: A viable narrow audio-focused option for known formats; not sufficient as the sole unknown-codec intake gate. Never supply guessed RAW values.

sources.title: W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.released_version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation WCAG 2.2, 2023-10-05
sources.locator: Success Criteria 2.1.1 Keyboard; 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap; 2.4.7 Focus Visible; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 4.1.3 Status Messages.
sources.accessed_utc: 2026-10-12T00:31:25Z/2026-10-12T00:42:08Z (first read through the later exact-criterion lookup; individual web-call timestamps unavailable)
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C Recommendation and its understanding page for status messages; read criterion text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Keyboard success criterion requires all functionality by keyboard; status messages in markup must be programmatically determinable without focus; criterion levels vary (2.1.1 A, 4.1.3 AA).
sources.applicability: Use for web UI; if target is native desktop, map to native accessibility APIs and test equivalent behaviors rather than claim WCAG markup conformance.

sources.title: BagIt File Packaging Format v1.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, published October 2018 (Informational RFC).
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and read structure, payload manifest, validation, and path-safety provisions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bag is a directory containing tags plus data/; payload is opaque bytes; manifests list every payload file and checksum. A checksum must be validated before declaring a bag valid. RFC warns path inputs must not escape the bag.
sources.applicability: Candidate portable handoff package; still needs catalog owner acceptance and safe path validation. It does not define transcript or rights semantics.

sources.title: W3C Web Audio API 1.1
sources.released_version_or_commit: Web Audio API 1.1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
sources.locator: MediaElementAudioSourceNode; ChannelSplitterNode overview and Section 1.15 interface (including active outputs per input channel).
sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C technical report; opened and read channel routing sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A ChannelSplitterNode provides outputs for the input stream's individual channels, e.g. two active outputs for stereo. It operates on an audio stream supplied to the graph and does not itself guarantee that the browser can decode every source format.
sources.applicability: If the UI is web-based, channel audition can be routed live without writing a converted media file when the browser decodes the original. This does not solve unsupported-codec preview; other UI targets need equivalent backend research.

sources.title: W3C WebVTT 1 timed text specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: WebVTT 1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
sources.locator: Cue timing syntax and rule that cue timestamps are interpreted relative to current playback position; lines 888-905.
sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C report; opened and read cue time and synchronization provisions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A timed cue has a start and end timestamp relative to the media playback timeline. Plain transcript text without cue times has no such synchronization data.
sources.applicability: Preserve supplied timing if present in a supported format; do not infer timings or require synchronized transcript preview absent an owner requirement.

sources.title: SQLite transaction control documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current SQLite transaction documentation accessed 2026-10-12; living documentation, no release/commit pinned.
sources.locator: Transactions; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; single simultaneous writer; SQLITE_BUSY conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened official SQLite documentation; read transaction behavior and busy conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A BEGIN...COMMIT transaction groups database changes; SQLite allows only one simultaneous write transaction and COMMIT/BEGIN IMMEDIATE can report SQLITE_BUSY. The transaction does not include copied media or an external catalog.
sources.applicability: Candidate local per-item checkpoint store; recovery must also reconcile the copied file and any later catalog import by hash/idempotency key.

critic_sources.title: HTML Standard — media element error example
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: WHATWG HTML Living Standard; page states last updated 2026-10-09; living standard, no commit
critic_sources.locator: Section 4.8.8 media-element error example, visible lines 325-342; the branches for MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED, MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK, MEDIA_ERR_DECODE, and MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened the official standard, inspected its error example and compared the cause branches. No browser or media test was run.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The example assigns separate messages to abort, network, decode (corruption or unsupported browser feature), and source-not-supported (server/network or unsupported format). This is a web-media example; some categories themselves admit multiple causes.
critic_sources.applicability: Shows why a player failure alone does not prove unreadable source bytes or unsupported format. It does not define every browser/player implementation or native-client diagnostics.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: corruption problem

critic_sources.title: Web Audio API 1.1
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: W3C Web Audio API 1.1 technical report; no repository commit
critic_sources.locator: Sections 1.15 ChannelSplitterNode and 1.22 MediaElementAudioSourceNode; active splitter outputs, channel count, routing, and channel-order note.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened the W3C report, located and read the splitter and media-element source sections. No audio was decoded or routed.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A MediaElementAudioSourceNode outputs the media element's channel count into the Web Audio graph; a ChannelSplitterNode exposes active outputs for input channels and preserves their order without assigning semantic identities.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports web-only feasibility of separate channel audition after the browser can decode the original. It neither guarantees codec support nor specifies native-player routing.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: number of channels in the input audio stream

critic_sources.title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: WebVTT 1 W3C technical report; current report page, no repository commit
critic_sources.locator: Cue block and cue timings definitions around section 4.4, visible lines 881-905; required start/end offsets and playback-position interpretation.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened the W3C report and read cue timing definitions and timestamp interpretation. No transcript was converted or synchronized.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A WebVTT cue timing has start and end offsets; timestamps are interpreted relative to the current playback position of the media to be synchronized.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports preserving supplied WebVTT cue timing. It does not define timing semantics for plain text or every transcript format, and does not justify synthesizing cue times.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: always interpreted relative to the current playback position

critic_sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 8493 / BagIt 1.0, published October 2018
critic_sources.locator: Sections 2.1.2-2.1.3 and 3, visible lines 375-405 and 755-775; payload directory, manifests, complete/valid bag definitions.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and inspected payload, manifest, completeness, and validity provisions.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BagIt requires a data/ payload directory and at least one payload manifest; every payload file is listed in each payload manifest. A valid bag must be complete and have checksums verified for every payload and tag manifest present.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports a checksummed opaque-byte package as a candidate. It does not decide the museum catalog's acceptance, rights meaning, transcript schema, or which payload files the receiver needs.

critic_sources.title: SQLite Transaction
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: Current SQLite transaction documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; living documentation, no commit
critic_sources.locator: Sections 2 and 2.1-2.3, visible lines 30-57; BEGIN/COMMIT nesting, single-writer behavior, and SQLITE_BUSY examples.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite's official transaction documentation and read transaction lifetime, writer, and busy conditions.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEGIN...COMMIT transactions do not nest; SQLite permits one simultaneous writer; competing access or pending readers/writers can cause SQLITE_BUSY. Database transactions cover database state only.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as one local checkpoint option and retry handling. It does not make file copying or import into an external catalog atomic.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: only one simultaneous write transaction

sources.title: BagIt File Packaging Format v1.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, published October 2018 (Informational RFC).
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and read structure, payload manifest, validation, and path-safety provisions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bag is a directory containing tags plus data/; payload is opaque bytes; manifests list every payload file and checksum. A checksum must be validated before declaring a bag valid. RFC warns path inputs must not escape the bag.
sources.applicability: Candidate portable handoff package; still needs catalog owner acceptance and safe path validation. It does not define transcript or rights semantics.

sources.title: W3C Web Audio API 1.1
sources.released_version_or_commit: Web Audio API 1.1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
sources.locator: MediaElementAudioSourceNode; ChannelSplitterNode overview and Section 1.15 interface (including active outputs per input channel).
sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C technical report; opened and read channel routing sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A ChannelSplitterNode provides outputs for the input stream's individual channels, e.g. two active outputs for stereo. It operates on an audio stream supplied to the graph and does not itself guarantee that the browser can decode every source format.
sources.applicability: If the UI is web-based, channel audition can be routed live without writing a converted media file when the browser decodes the original. This does not solve unsupported-codec preview; other UI targets need equivalent backend research.

sources.title: W3C WebVTT 1 timed text specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: WebVTT 1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
sources.locator: Cue timing syntax and rule that cue timestamps are interpreted relative to current playback position; lines 888-905.
sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C report; opened and read cue time and synchronization provisions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A timed cue has a start and end timestamp relative to the media playback timeline. Plain transcript text without cue times has no such synchronization data.
sources.applicability: Preserve supplied timing if present in a supported format; do not infer timings or require synchronized transcript preview absent an owner requirement.

sources.title: SQLite transaction control documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current SQLite transaction documentation accessed 2026-10-12; living documentation, no release/commit pinned.
sources.locator: Transactions; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; single simultaneous writer; SQLITE_BUSY conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened official SQLite documentation; read transaction behavior and busy conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A BEGIN...COMMIT transaction groups database changes; SQLite allows only one simultaneous write transaction and COMMIT/BEGIN IMMEDIATE can report SQLITE_BUSY. The transaction does not include copied media or an external catalog.
sources.applicability: Candidate local per-item checkpoint store; recovery must also reconcile the copied file and any later catalog import by hash/idempotency key.

inherited_sources.applicability: Candidate portable handoff package; still needs catalog owner acceptance and safe path validation. It does not define transcript or rights semantics.

inherited_sources.title: W3C Web Audio API 1.1
inherited_sources.released_version_or_commit: Web Audio API 1.1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
inherited_sources.locator: MediaElementAudioSourceNode; ChannelSplitterNode overview and Section 1.15 interface (including active outputs per input channel).
inherited_sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C technical report; opened and read channel routing sections.
inherited_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A ChannelSplitterNode provides outputs for the input stream's individual channels, e.g. two active outputs for stereo. It operates on an audio stream supplied to the graph and does not itself guarantee that the browser can decode every source format.
inherited_sources.applicability: If the UI is web-based, channel audition can be routed live without writing a converted media file when the browser decodes the original. This does not solve unsupported-codec preview; other UI targets need equivalent backend research.

inherited_sources.title: W3C WebVTT 1 timed text specification
inherited_sources.released_version_or_commit: WebVTT 1 W3C technical report; current report page accessed 2026-10-12, no repository commit.
inherited_sources.locator: Cue timing syntax and rule that cue timestamps are interpreted relative to current playback position; lines 888-905.
inherited_sources.observed_operation: Searched W3C report; opened and read cue time and synchronization provisions.
inherited_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A timed cue has a start and end timestamp relative to the media playback timeline. Plain transcript text without cue times has no such synchronization data.
inherited_sources.applicability: Preserve supplied timing if present in a supported format; do not infer timings or require synchronized transcript preview absent an owner requirement.

inherited_sources.title: SQLite transaction control documentation
inherited_sources.released_version_or_commit: Current SQLite transaction documentation accessed 2026-10-12; living documentation, no release/commit pinned.
inherited_sources.locator: Transactions; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; single simultaneous writer; SQLITE_BUSY conditions.
inherited_sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened official SQLite documentation; read transaction behavior and busy conditions.
inherited_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A BEGIN...COMMIT transaction groups database changes; SQLite allows only one simultaneous write transaction and COMMIT/BEGIN IMMEDIATE can report SQLITE_BUSY. The transaction does not include copied media or an external catalog.
inherited_sources.applicability: Candidate local per-item checkpoint store; recovery must also reconcile the copied file and any later catalog import by hash/idempotency key.

critic_sources.title: HTML Standard — media element error example

critic_sources.locator: Section 4.8.8 media-element error example, visible lines 325-342; the branches for MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED, MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK, MEDIA_ERR_DECODE, and MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened the official standard, inspected its error example and compared the cause branches. No browser or media test was run.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The example assigns separate messages to abort, network, decode (corruption or unsupported browser feature), and source-not-supported (server/network or unsupported format). This is a web-media example; some categories themselves admit multiple causes.
critic_sources.applicability: Shows why a player failure alone does not prove unreadable source bytes or unsupported format. It does not define every browser/player implementation or native-client diagnostics.

critic_sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 8493 / BagIt 1.0, published October 2018
critic_sources.locator: Sections 2.1.2-2.1.3 and 3, visible lines 375-405 and 755-775; payload directory, manifests, complete/valid bag definitions.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and inspected payload, manifest, completeness, and validity provisions.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BagIt requires a data/ payload directory and at least one payload manifest; every payload file is listed in each payload manifest. A valid bag must be complete and have checksums verified for every payload and tag manifest present.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports a checksummed opaque-byte package as a candidate. It does not decide the museum catalog's acceptance, rights meaning, transcript schema, or which payload files the receiver needs.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: Every checksum in every payload manifest and tag manifest has been successfully verified against the contents of the corresponding file.

critic_sources.title: SQLite Transaction
critic_sources.released_version_or_commit: Current SQLite transaction documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; living documentation, no commit
critic_sources.locator: Sections 2 and 2.1-2.3, visible lines 30-57; BEGIN/COMMIT nesting, single-writer behavior, and SQLITE_BUSY examples.
critic_sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite's official transaction documentation and read transaction lifetime, writer, and busy conditions.
critic_sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEGIN...COMMIT transactions do not nest; SQLite permits one simultaneous writer; competing access or pending readers/writers can cause SQLITE_BUSY. Database transactions cover database state only.
critic_sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as one local checkpoint option and retry handling. It does not make file copying or import into an external catalog atomic.
critic_sources.scope_bearing_excerpt: only one simultaneous write transaction
